'''Harris Pastides''' (born 1954) is an academic and university administrator who served as the 28th president of the [[University of South Carolina]] from 2008 until 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://chronicle.augusta.com/news/education/2012-10-06/university-south-carolina-president-harris-pastides-receive-21-percent-pay|title=University of South Carolina president Harris Pastides to receive 21 percent pay raise|access-date=2016-11-24}}</ref> In addition to his employment at the university Pastides has been on the [[board of directors]] of [[Synovus]], a financial services company.<ref>{{Cite web|title=404 Page Not Found &#124; SNL Financial LC|url=http://www.snl.com/Cache/c397084070.html|access-date=2022-03-07|website=www.snl.com|archive-date=June 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190617122921/http://www.snl.com/Cache/c397084070.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 3, 2018, Pastides announced his intention to retire from the presidency of USC, the last day of which he served on July 31, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thestate.com/news/local/education/article219379990.html|title=USC President Harris Pastides announces plans to step down|work=thestate|access-date=2018-10-03|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Gatson|first=Judi|title=Pastides reflects on his legacy, leaves advice for his successor, and reveals plans for the future|url=https://www.wistv.com/2019/08/01/pastides-reflects-his-legacy-leaves-advice-his-successor-reveals-plans-future/|access-date=2022-03-07|website=www.wistv.com|date=August 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He was again appointed Interim President at South Carolina after [[Robert L. Caslen|Bob Caslen]] resigned on May 13, 2021, officially taking office May 21, 2021 and serving until July 1, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wistv.com/2021/05/12/uofsc-president-resign-may/|title=UofSC president announces resignation, effective May 13|date=May 21, 2021 }}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Pastides was born in the New York City borough of [[Queens]] to immigrants from [[Cyprus]]. He was the first person in his family to attend college when he enrolled in the [[University at Albany]] where he obtained his [[B.S.]] in Biology. He received his master's in public health and his M.Phil. and Ph.D. in [[epidemiology]] from [[Yale University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thestate.com/news/politics-government/article14440685.html|title=A day in the life of USC's president|last=Shain |first=Andrew|access-date=2016-11-24}}</ref>

He began his academic career at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where during 1980–1998, he rose to become professor of epidemiology and chairman of the Department of Biostatistics and Epidemiology.<ref>{{cite web|title=CV last updated on Wednesday, May 17, 2017|url=https://sam.research.sc.edu/uscera/facultyExpertise/cv/3011}}</ref> In 2008, he was a finalist to become the university's Chancellor.<ref>{{cite web|title=Search Committee Names Four Finalists for UMass Amherst Chancellorship|url=https://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/search-committee-names-four-finalists-umass-amherst-chancellorship|access-date=December 31, 2019|archive-date=December 31, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231232928/https://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/search-committee-names-four-finalists-umass-amherst-chancellorship|url-status=dead}}</ref> His study on the health effects of chemicals used by the US semiconductor industry revealed links to an increase in miscarriages among employees. Although initially resisted, the study's findings were subsequently borne out, ironically leading to chipmaking's eventual outsourcing overseas.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Simpson|first1=Cam|title=American Chipmakers Had a Toxic Problem. Then They Outsourced It |newspaper=Bloomberg.com |date=June 15, 2017 |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2017-06-15/american-chipmakers-had-a-toxic-problem-so-they-outsourced-it |publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|accessdate=June 16, 2017}}</ref>

==President of the University of South Carolina==
[[File:President of U of SC, Harris Pastides.jpg|thumb|left|President Pastides at [[South Carolina Gamecocks women's basketball|Women's Basketball]] national championship parade, 2022.]]
His election by the board of trustees marks the first internal candidate for the presidency of the university in more than a half century. Previously, Pastides served as vice president for research and health sciences and dean of the Arnold School of Public Health.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mycarolina.org/s/842/site2014/interior-1col-noname.aspx?sid=842&gid=1&pgid=6766&sparam=Harris%20Pastides&scontid=0|title=Harris Pastides|website=www.mycarolina.org|access-date=2016-11-24}}{{Dead link|date=December 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He and his wife, Patricia, first came to the university in 1998.

During his tenure, Carolina's student population grew to record levels among the system's eight universities on 12 campuses. On the notion that degree attainment significantly affects the quality of life in [[South Carolina]], Pastides lead nontraditional programs such as [[Palmetto College]], Back to Carolina, Gamecock Gateway and Gamecock Guarantee to increase university access and affordability. In addition, he led a capital campaign to fund university priorities.

In addition to his position as President of the university, since 2014, Pastides has held a secondary employment in the private sector as part of the financial services industry. He has received $161,700 a year in stock and cash as a [[board of directors|director]] at [[Synovus]], a publicly traded financial services corporation specializing in commercial loans, mortgages, and retail banking.<ref>{{Cite web|title=404 Page Not Found &#124; SNL Financial LC|url=http://www.snl.com/Cache/c397084070.html|access-date=2022-03-07|website=www.snl.com|archive-date=June 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190617122921/http://www.snl.com/Cache/c397084070.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The [[South Carolina Gamecocks women's basketball|University of South Carolina's women's basketball team]] won two national championships during his presidency, once in 2017 and again in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Subhan |first1=Amna |title=South Carolina wins 2022 DI women's basketball national championship |url=https://www.ncaa.com/live-updates/basketball-women/d1/south-carolina-wins-2022-di-womens-basketball-national-championship |website=NCAA |access-date=25 July 2022}}</ref>

Following the [[murder of Samantha Josephson]], a university student who mistakenly entered the wrong car she believed to be her [[Uber]] and was killed, Pastides, along with Josephson's parents, popularized the phrase: "What's my name?" Pastides stated, "These three words have the power to save lives and must become as automatic to every college student getting into a ride-hailing vehicle as putting on a seatbelt."<ref name="Pastides">{{cite news |last1=Pastides |first1=Harris |title=Three words to help avoid the tragedy of mistaking a killer's car for your Uber |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2019/04/08/three-words-help-avoid-tragedy-mistaking-killers-car-your-uber/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=25 July 2022}}</ref> Pastides further advocated for further legislation to regulate the rideshare business, which was signed by Governor [[Henry McMaster]] as the Samantha L. Josephson Ridesharing Safety Act the following month.<ref>{{cite web |title=Samantha L. Josephson Ridesharing Safety Act |url=https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess123_2019-2020/bills/4380.htm |website=sc.gov |publisher=State of South Carolina}}</ref>

On October 3, 2018, Pastides announced his plan to retire as president from the university.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-10-03|title=University of S Carolina President Pastides to retire|url=https://apnews.com/article/b221c93d919c49cbbc291f72792b44b2|access-date=2022-03-07|website=AP NEWS|language=en}}</ref> Shortly before, a report prepared by special prosecutor David Pascoe had revealed that several major South Carolina institutions, including the University of South Carolina, had used the Quinn firm to lobby the legislature while the firm was secretly paying S.C. lawmakers to influence legislation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=S.C. universities paying lobbyists as student tuition, school debt loads rise » The Nerve|url=https://thenerve.org/2018/10/s-c-universities-paying-lobbyists-as-student-tuition-school-debt-loads-rise/|access-date=2022-03-07|website=thenerve.org|date=October 17, 2018 }}</ref> Following a contentious search to hire a new USC President, former [[Superintendent of the United States Military Academy|Superintendent]] of West Point [[Robert L. Caslen]] was eventually selected as Pastides' successor and took office on August 1, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/university-of-south-carolina-trustees-vote-for-governors-pick-for-president/|access-date=2022-03-07|website=www.chronicle.com}}</ref>

===Interim President===
The Board of Trustees appointed Pastides as Interim President of the University of South Carolina after his successor, [[Robert L. Caslen|Bob Caslen]], resigned on May 13, 2021. Pastides held the role from May 21, 2021 to July 1, 2022. He was succeeded by [[Michael Amiridis]].
